elements.content: Grammar focus: Reporting Verbs.

Choose the verb for the attitude first, then follow its pattern. If you are unsure of the pattern, use the that-clause, which nearly all reporting verbs accept. Keep the negative before the infinitive: warned us not to sign.

verb + -ing — admit, deny, suggest, recommend: she admitted taking the file
verb + to-infinitive — agree, refuse, offer, promise: they refused to sign
verb + object + to-infinitive — warn, persuade, remind, urge: he warned us not to sign
verb + preposition + -ing — insist on, object to, apologise for: insisted on a written reply
verb + that-clause — safe option for most verbs: she admitted that she had taken the file
verb + object + of — accuse, suspect: they accused him of leaking the file
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'She admitted ___ the email.'
2. Complete: 'They refused ___ the offer.'
3. Complete: 'He warned us ___ the file.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

She admitted taking the file. — Verb + -ing. (Admit, deny, suggest, recommend.)
He warned us not to sign. — Verb + object + to-infinitive. (Warn, persuade, remind, urge.)
The chair insisted on a written reply. — Verb + preposition + noun or -ing. (Insist on, apologise for, object to.)
What do you observe?

Reporting verbs carry the speaker's attitude and each has its own pattern. Admit, deny, suggest, recommend and regret take the -ing form. Agree, refuse, offer, promise and threaten take the to-infinitive. Warn, persuade, remind and urge take an object plus the to-infinitive. Insist on, object to, apologise for and accuse of take a preposition. Many also accept a that-clause, which is the safest option when the pattern is uncertain.
1. Which pattern does deny take?
2. Which verb takes an object plus the to-infinitive?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can use say and tell correctly.

Success criteria:
- I can use -ing after admit, deny and suggest.
- I can use object plus to-infinitive after warn and remind.
- I can use the that-clause when the pattern is uncertain.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ They denied to have seen it (infinitive after deny) → ✅ They denied having seen it
❌ He warned us to not sign (split negative in the wrong place) → ✅ He warned us not to sign
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The supplier admitted shipping the wrong batch.
The board denied authorising the payment.
The auditors warned the team against early sign-off.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where reporting verbs carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
